A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RWNN research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across renaming, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-isomorphism classification, graph-level and vertex-level 8-cycle counting, and ogbn-arxiv classification results in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds random-walk simulations, synthetic regression, additional real-world benchmarks, fine-tuning experiments, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices A.4–A.8.

M1.justification: The core walk and recording Algorithms 1–4 are retained. v2 adds limited procedural adaptations: scalar-feature records that repeat the queried vertex's value (A.4), QLoRA fine-tuning of the Llama3-8b reader (A.6), and link prediction through vertex classification on line graphs (A.7).

E1.justification: v2 retains the original datasets and tasks while adding lollipop cover-time simulations, Clique/Barbell scalar regression, Cora/Citeseer/Amazon Ratings node classification, Peptides-func molecular graph classification, and YST/KHN/ADV link prediction. These substantially broaden task requirements and coverage of attributed, homophilic, and heterophilic graphs.

E2.justification: GraphSAGE is added to the retained ogbn-arxiv comparison. New comparisons include NSD, BuNN, WalkLM-transformer, and CRaWl variants on Clique/Barbell; GraphText, LLaGA, and OFA on additional classification datasets; and Katz, PR, SR, SEAL, and LGLP for link prediction. The original isomorphism and counting comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce substantial new evaluation designs, including 500-epoch Adam training with learning rate 1e-4 and batch size 1 on Clique/Barbell, small transformer configurations, AP evaluation for peptide classification and link prediction, and controlled pretraining, walk-length, restart-rate, and ensemble-size comparisons. The documented original isomorphism and counting protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained attention visualizations, v2 adds direct cover-time and propagation tests, pretrained-versus-random initialization experiments (Figure 14), named-neighbor removal on SR16 (Table 11), restart-rate comparisons on arXiv (Table 12), and ensemble-size sweeps (Table 13). These test mechanisms and design choices that v1 did not ablate.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates and prediction-ensemble sizes without empirical uncertainty estimates. v2 adds four-run synthetic and three-run link-prediction aggregations, mean and standard deviation over five Peptides-func tests, and uncertainty in ensemble-size experiments. Tables 5 and 13 explicitly identify unavailable repeated evaluations. This introduces statistical reporting rather than establishing an increase over previously specified run counts.

E6.justification: The original isomorphism accuracies and 8-cycle MAEs are retained in v2 Tables 3 and 9. Several ogbn-arxiv values change: Llama3-8b zero-shot changes from 50.20% to 51.31%, and the 70b RWNN using validation labels changes from 74.75% to 74.85%; these are not established as controlled performance gains. Substantial new results include fine-tuned arXiv accuracy of 74.95%, Peptides-func AP of 0.7123 ± 0.0016, and synthetic, link-prediction, and ablation outcomes.

T1.justification: The invariance results, universality definitions, cover-time bounds, restart arguments, and propagation theorems retain the same mathematical substance and proofs, with v1 A.4 corresponding to v2 A.9. Relabeling several theorems as propositions and clarifying probabilistic notation do not introduce substantive theoretical changes.

C1.justification: v2 more explicitly claims a unifying formalization and principled analysis of the existing RWNN family, whereas v1 foregrounds the proposed RWNN approach and its language-model demonstrations. It also moderates the arXiv comparison to competitive performance against a range of MPNNs. The central invariance, universality, propagation, SR25, and training-free classification claims persist.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of language-pretraining benefits and ensemble scaling, distinguishes worst-case cover-time guarantees from useful information obtainable without full coverage, and explicitly limits the propagation analysis mainly to fixed-weight MPNNs, excluding attention-based variants. The brief computational-cost limitation is expanded with measured inference costs and practical comparisons (A.5, A.8, A.10–A.11).

D1.justification: v2 newly documents arXiv restart probability 0.7 selected using 100 validation examples, its 4,096-token input cap, new task encoders and training details, link-prediction restart period 5, and inference timings on four H100 GPUs. These are substantial disclosures, not evidence that previously unspecified settings changed. The code URL is retained, while v1's eight-RTX-3090 training disclosure and SR25 baseline-configuration note are dropped.

R1.justification: v2 adds a framework taxonomy in Table 1, connections to invariant projection and frame averaging through Puny et al. (2022) and Dym et al. (2024), and discussion of concurrent Wang and Cho (2024). Appendix A.10 substantially expands the distinctions from Micali–Zhu reconstruction and CRaWl's windowed encodings, and discusses adaptive message passing.

P1.justification: The introduction is extensively rewritten around three research questions and an explicit contributions narrative, with standardized RWNN/MPNN/MDLR terminology. The experimental narrative now starts with synthetic validation; counting moves to A.7, proofs to A.9, and extended related work and limitations occupy A.10–A.11. The abstract and conclusion are also substantially rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds the method overview table, cover-time and walk-length plots, pretraining curves, a peptide-record illustration, and numerous benchmark and ablation tables. Retained displays are reformatted, the arXiv table groups methods differently, and the counting table moves to the appendix within the new conference layout.

improvement.justification: v1 provides substantial theory but little direct empirical testing of its design rationale. v2 addresses this important gap through cover-time and propagation experiments, pretraining and recording ablations, and restart and ensemble analyses. Broader real-world evaluations, uncertainty reporting, and clearer computational and theoretical limitations substantially strengthen the evidence and its interpretation. These gains outweigh the loss of some earlier configuration and hardware disclosures; the small arXiv score revisions are not the basis for this assessment.
